note_tweet.text:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

note_tweet.text:
My thought on the role of growth in solving fiscal problems:

1. I'm in favor of dynamic scoring for both tax & spending plans--you should take into account the best estimate of impact on budget.

2. Dynamic scoring needs to be done by CBO/JCT, they're generally unbiased and reasonably efficient. As a result they often disappoint advocates.

3. Ideally CBO would also display other information than just growth, the sole goal of every policy is not necessarily growth, it might also be about providing health insurance or increasing national security.

4. Dynamic scoring will usually be small relative to the first order effects of policies on spending and taxes.

5. I wouldn't overthink the second-order political incentives and impacts, if you have good information you'll generally (but not always) have better policy.

article.plain_text:
Earlier last week I posted my calculation that went viral that projected so much compute coming online next year per SemiAnalysis power availability data, that we would need 2.5T revenue to consume all that, even assuming only 50% of compute for inference at - wait for it - DeepSeek V4.1 Flash rates.

I have been running the numbers again and again and have realised the numbers are even more insane than I initially calculated on basis of SemiAnalysis power addition projection, and DS Flash inference economics validated by vLLM and SGLang teams!!!
There is too much compute coming online. However, proponents of Jevon's paradox have a great track record. This is sincere attempt to see both side of the arguments by modeling the scenarios. Please do review and let me know what you think.
What changes?
* SemiAnalysis 50 GW power number for 2027 was net new addition and not cumulative power. So that much power will be available by end of 2027.
* So cumulative power from 2025 - which is mostly for AI - is 91.6 GW by end of 2027 (Astra has the same interpretation after seeing the article. SemiAnalysis team, please correct me if I got it wrong).
 
Source Article: https://newsletter.semianalysis.com/p/datacenters-2027-the-year-of-acceleration
Assuming there are enough accelerators to consume all that capacity (there are per SemiAnalysis at least in 2027), total revenue projection at revenue rate of 100B / GW for 2027 are insane at 4.5T USD. And remember we are assuming DS Flash prices in this analysis which with their architecture and efficiency offers 100B USD revenue per GW even assuming lot of slack.
See the chart to see projections for 2025, 2026 and 2027. From 2025 to 2027 we are assuming inference increasing from 10% to 50% overall compute and revenue per GW rising from 20B/GW to 100B/GW.
 
Does it mean we would have a massive glut? 
Not necessarily.

1. Lot of supply could be consumed for demand that can not be measured in token revenue (e.g. Google search, Meta Muse)
2. There might be massive collapse in token prices reducing per GW revenue from 100B / GW to something like 20B / GW (with that overall token dollar value goes from 4.5T to approximately 1T USD. In that case the global economy 'may' be able to absorb the supply, otherwise not.). But this model is based on 20% of DS Flash pricing!!! Compared to OpenAI and Anthropic pricing, this is ridiculously low already. To reach those levels the leading US labs may have to cut prices by 20 times.
3. Models may become so cheap, we may use large models for everything (why use Haiku class models when you can use Fable Opus/Opus for everything).
4. Most models may get served at high interactivity at low batch sizes. Why not everyone gets 'FAST', if there is capacity!
5. This may enable new application (real time voice assistant that are every expensive at 3$ per hr,  digital companions, personalised entertainment, robotics etc. Global education industry will completely get transformed). However, existing labs like Anthropic and OpenAI are not yet interested in this space, certainly not beyond robotics and use of their models in education. This is a massive opportunity for the startups in the space.
6. 'Continuously on' cyber security may consume a decent amount capacity as well (not only design time reviews, but theorem proving, run time security etc.)
However, there are too many variable that need to fall in place for this capacity to be absorbed so rapidly - there are only 15 month, and so it is not guaranteed. Probability of it not happening (absorption) is far higher that it getting absorbed.
What about training costs?
Also, we are assuming 50% of total capacity that is 45.9GW (capacity costing 459 B a year at 10B/GW) for training. Recall Anthropic till date since its foundation has spend just under 16B USD on model training & research (interpretability). 16B was enough to get you from Claude 2 all the way to current generation with all the model lineages: Mythos, Fable, Opus, Sonnet and Haiku. I find it hard to believe that for major labs put together - Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepMind, MSL and xAI -  training expense to run 459B ARR by end of the next year end. I suspect most of the compute would have to be absorbed by free services like Google Search and Meta Muse.
What if prices and demand adjust the compute supply & Jevon's paradox plays out by end of 2027?
While this low probability scenario, it is still likely. If token prices and demand adjust to consume available capacity we would see following:
LLM Model prices with respect to intelligence would be down by around  20 times (this would be in line with the trend predicted by EpochAI). I am assuming tough competition between leading labs eroding pricing power, as it is hard to form oligopoly when there are 5 players in the market, and it is also illegal.
Model lab profit margins will have collapsed from 70-90% to below 30-20%. Not bad because volume would be enormous - approximately 1 T USD ARR by 2027 end. They will be roughly making  20B USD/GW and paying 10B USD/GW to hyperscalars.  They will cut down on training costs and inference may be more than 50% of compute use (we assumed 50% in this article for 2027, if you recall). Saving on training costs is the only way to hit 30-20% profit margins with such low rates. 
Remaining compute after LLM labs squeeze of training would be used by Search, Muse and personal experience (companions, entertainment) & Robotics. I expect golden age of AI powered startups that are model builders as well.
Labs will negotiate hard with hyperscalars to cut down per GW cost to below 10B USD/GW. Hyperscalars will negotiate hard, in turn, to cut prices for semiconductors. Hyperscalars have advantage of scale and custom silicon program, so this may be disadvantage Neo-Clouds (at least long tail ones).
Efficient use of electricity and efficient chips would be paramount from hyper-scalar perspective at they try to reduce compute rental cost. We will see advantage for vendors offering that. We will see further emphasis on ASIC programs to cut rental of 1GW of compute to below 10B USD/GW by avoiding Nvidia tax. We will see lot of interest in both: Mature silicon that offers high amount tokens / MW (advantage Nvidia) as well as new approaches that avoid Nvidia tax and reduce power demand (OpenAI Jalapeno)
Global AI revenue (ex-China, as SemiAnalysis numbers are ex-China) would be approximately 1T USD per year by end of 2027 in this modal, requiring 147 USD revenue from every living human (on average). Hard but not impossible given average GDP per capita ex-China is 14,518$. So this is 1% of that, and people spend more than that amount on telephone services.
 
However, the real issue is capacity does not stop coming online in 2027, it keeps on getting added in 2028, 2029, 2030 and so on; and chips last really long. All the valuations are built on this assumption that 1T USD buildout and spend will continue in perpetuity. Hence, I am calling out AI overbuilding and requesting you to think how hard it is to consume all the capacity.

I may be wrong and will change my opinion, if I see a better argument. But I am afraid we are into full blown overbuilding phase.
